findings.description: Docs and ADR 0200 say an `autoCompactWindow` or other rule edit reaches a window at its next respawn, but `relaunchWindow` reuses the stored `compiled/settings.json` and recompiles nothing, so a respawn keeps the old window (or none).
findings.body:
**A respawn does not apply an `autoCompactWindow` edit, but the docs say it does.**

`docs/03-profiles.md` says "An edit takes effect at the next launch or respawn, never in a window already open." ADR 0200's "When respawn is still the right tool" list also gives "a change of rules: a profile, brief or project-config edit, the compaction window included, lands only in a freshly compiled window" as a reason to run `pup respawn` (<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ab5f27200b8eaeebdbcd17f53b5c9951fee53721/docs/adr/0200-compaction-is-the-default-context-reset-respawn-is.md#L44-L49>).

A respawn compiles nothing. `relaunchWindow` reads the stored `context.md` and launches with the settings already on disk:

```ts
settingsPath: join(compiledDir, 'settings.json'),
```
<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ab5f27200b8eaeebdbcd17f53b5c9951fee53721/src/core/session-handoff.service.ts#L286-L337>

Every respawn entry point goes through it: `pup respawn`, `pup kill --respawn` and the UI action. Only a fresh launch and a `pup fix` round (`recompileSessionProfile`) recompile. ADR 0183 already corrected this same claim ("a respawn resends the stored context and recompiles nothing"), and so does ADR 0115 ("only `pup fix` recompiles a profile").

What goes wrong:
- An operator edits `autoCompactWindow` in `.pupitre/project.yml` and runs `pup respawn <id>`, as the ADR advises. The new window still compacts at the old value.
- A session compiled before this PR has no `autoCompactWindow` at all. A respawn leaves it on the operator's user window, and `pup status` shows a bare `ctx ~Nk` for it.

The fix is to correct both passages to say the next launch or `pup fix` round. For example, in `docs/03-profiles.md`: "An edit takes effect at the next launch or `pup fix` round, never at a respawn, which reuses the stored settings, nor in a window already open." Then drop the project-config/compaction-window clause from ADR 0200's respawn list, or reword it the same way. The other option, making respawn recompile, would reverse earlier decisions and needs its own ADR.

findings.description: pup pins only `autoCompactWindow`: if the operator has turned auto-compact off (user settings or an inherited `DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT`), windows never compact, `pup status` prints `at compaction` indefinitely, and the removed 120k respawn hint no longer flags them; pinning auto-compact on in the compiled settings/env would close this.

`settingsFileOf` reads through a new `compiled/` path component: a session that replaces `compiled` with a regular file makes `openSync` fail with ENOTDIR, which `readSessionFile` rethrows, so one row marks the whole project unreadable; treating ENOTDIR like ENOENT/ELOOP keeps the cost to that row.

The window is accepted up to 1,000,000 whatever the routed model's context: with `autoCompactWindow: 300000` on a 200k-context model, Claude Code likely compacts near the model limit while `pup status` computes 267k and prints a distance that never arrives.
`left` is rounded before the `> 0` test, so a session 1–499 tokens short of its compaction point is labelled `at compaction` early; compare `compactAt > tokens` before rounding.

The `compactAtTokens` doc says it is absent only when the settings carry no window, but it is also absent with no context reading, a non-minted id, an unreadable or planted file, or an out-of-range window.

`readSessionFile`'s doc now covers the settings file too, but still says a planted link "costs its row the activity"; for the settings file it costs the compaction hint, so "costs its row that reading" fits both.

The conductor's comment "The project's window, as a worker's is (decision 200)" only points at the worker's comment, which carries the WHY; drop it or state the WHY (a flag settings file outranks the operator's).

process_issues.description: review-spec skipped: the PR names no closing issue, no --spec, and no closing keyword. review-workflow-safety skipped: no .github/workflows change. review-maintainability skipped: not on the standard roster. Dropped as below the finding bar: two simplicity nits whose reviewer conceded the construct was defensible (range re-check in compactionPoint; settingsFileOf mirroring eventsFileOf), and one docs nit on the contextLabel history sentence.

The validator for the auto-compact-disabled finding confirmed the mechanism but judged it an operator opt-out with only a misleading label, so I downgraded it from important to nit. Both validators reported `git diff`/`git show` calls blocked for approval; they used `gh pr diff` and head files instead.
